chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abd al-Wahhab ibn al-Subah from his father who said:

Muslim, the freedman of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), met Sadqah al-Ahdb, who had just returned from Mecca. So Muslim said to him: 'All praise is due to Allah, who made your path easy and guided your way, and brought you back in a state of health, having completed the Hajj and facilitated the ease [of travel]. May Allah accept from you, compensate your expenses, and make it a accepted Hajj and a purification for your sins.'

This reached Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he said to him: 'How did you say to Sadqah?' He repeated it to him. He said to him: 'Who taught you this?' He said: 'May I be your ransom, my Master Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him).' He said to him: 'Excellent is what you learned. When you meet a brother from among your brothers, say to him thus, for the guidance is with us [i.e., the Imams] is true guidance; and when you meet these [others], say to them what they say.'

key_terms.اَلْهُدَى بِنَا: The guidance is with us (the Imams)
key_terms.صَدَقَةَ اَلْأَحْدَبَ: Sadqah al-Ahdb, a companion of the Imams

ai.seo_question: What is the etiquette for greeting someone returning from Hajj according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the Shia principle of *al-Tawqi wa al-Taqiyya* (precision and caution) in social interactions, distinguishing between intimate spiritual bonds and general public discourse. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validated the specific, comprehensive supplication used for 'brothers' (those sharing the Ahl al-Bayt's guidance) while instructing to adopt the common, non-committal greetings of others to avoid theological ambiguity or political risk. This reflects the scholarly tradition of tailoring communication to the audience's level of understanding and context.
